A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Thought-Aligner. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of Thought-Aligner on ToolEmu, PrivacyLens and Agent-SafetyBench, including thought-correction and failure-mode analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark evaluations, thought-level validation, training ablations, latency measurements and qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5 backbones, two-stage likelihood training and thought-correction/action-regeneration loop remain unchanged. V3 Section 4.2 adds a limited adaptation for reasoning models: request an explicit Thought field or summarize a reasoning trace before correction. Algorithm 1 otherwise documents the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V3 retains ToolEmu and Agent-SafetyBench, removes dedicated PrivacyLens evaluation, and adds AgentHarm, AgentDojo and InjecAgent evaluations covering malicious requests and prompt-injection settings. Its training description also explicitly includes adversarial trajectory conditions. The ten underlying training risk categories remain substantially unchanged, including the renamed Physical Risk category.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates ATHENA against Thought-Aligner on ToolEmu and uses undefended comparisons elsewhere. V3 adds Self-Reflection, GuardAgent and ShieldAgent, and evaluates ATHENA on Agent-SafetyBench too. Tables 3-4 additionally compare single-stage SFT, small-model reflection and four general-purpose LLMs used directly as thought correctors.

E3.justification: V3 replaces the benchmark-specific agent configurations with six newer backbones. ToolEmu's stated simulator/evaluator change from GPT-3.5-Turbo/GPT-4-Turbo to DeepSeek-V3, and ATHENA's critic becomes GPT-4.1. Training synthesis expands from one generator and 5,000 instructions to four generators and over 20,000 instructions, with substantially larger training sets. New experiments introduce classification metrics, controlled training comparisons and benchmark-specific safety/helpfulness conversions.

E4.justification: V3 adds thought-level classification validation, two-stage versus single-stage training ablations, comparisons with untrained thought correctors, and two ToolEmu cases concerning sensitive disclosures. Conversely, v1's ten-failure-mode analysis and improvement summaries in Tables 11-12 disappear. The semantic visualization and dataset examples are retained rather than newly introduced analyses.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without uncertainty bars. V3 Appendix C adds bootstrap/error bars to ToolEmu and Agent-SafetyBench summaries in Figures 10-14. Resampling counts, interval coverage, repeated-run counts and seeds remain unspecified; this establishes additional uncertainty reporting, not additional independent runs.

E6.justification: V3 substantially replaces the benchmark result set and removes PrivacyLens and ten-failure-mode results. New results include DeepSeek-V3 AgentHarm safety of 42.8% without protection versus 89.3% with Thought-Aligner-7B, alongside helpfulness falling from 85.0% to 36.5% (Table 11). Table 4 adds 0.06/0.11-second latency measurements. Changed agents, training data and evaluators prevent interpreting these as matched-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The trajectory/MDP formulation and conditional likelihood objective retain their mathematical substance. Explicit action-input notation and expanded training notation restate existing operations. V3's causal framing and applicability qualifications introduce no new formal causal model, theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds safety improvement, including roughly 10 percentage points over ATHENA. V3 claims roughly 23 points over expanded baselines, adds an approximately 5-point helpfulness improvement claim, and emphasizes generalization across additional risk settings. It also restricts the introductory sub-100ms claim to the 1.5B model. These materially revise the empirical contribution while retaining the plug-in premise.

C2.justification: V3 expands the explanation of utility preservation through correction rather than blocking, while acknowledging conservative behavior on additional benchmarks. New discussion distinguishes interventionist from mechanistic causality, states dependence on the agent following corrected thoughts, explains Azure o3 filtering effects, and qualifies scaling and real-world applicability. V1 mainly discusses safety-helpfulness trade-offs and the requirement for explicit thoughts.

D1.justification: V3 adds integration pseudocode, heuristic/human filtering details and identification of t-SNE for the existing semantic visualization. The printed checkpoint reference changes from fgdrg/Thought-Aligner-7B-v1.0 to WhitzardAgent/Thought-Aligner-7B, while benchmark-code/license footnotes are removed. Detailed training hyperparameters and hardware remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V3 adds references and positioning involving AgentSentinel, Self-Reflection, AgentAuditor, t-SNE and real-world agent incidents, while dropping several general-agent citations. The basic contrast with external critics and rule-based guardrails remains. AgentHarm, AgentDojo and InjecAgent were already cited in v1; their new evaluation does not itself constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around three challenges and causal intervention. Training explanations are reorganized into explicit stages, and dedicated ablation, discussion/limitations and impact sections are added. The appendices are substantially reorganized, and author/affiliation information changes.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws the pipeline and score-distribution figures, and replaces the pooled safety-helpfulness scatter with model-specific panels. It restructures the principal results table, adds validation/ablation/latency tables and uncertainty/case figures, and removes PrivacyLens and failure-mode displays. Several dataset illustrations and the semantic plot are retained and relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v1's missing training ablations and limited efficiency evidence, and broadens guardrail comparisons. However, important new evidence is internally inconsistent: DeepSeek-V3 with Thought-Aligner-7B has 92.2% ToolEmu safety in Table 1 but 97.2% in Table 3; Llama-3.3-70B helpfulness is 39.6% in Table 1 but 59.7% in Table 4, without explained setting differences. These conflicts affect central safety and utility claims, preventing a reliable judgment that the added evidence produces a net quality improvement.
